answer: Every identity must lock a bond before it acts. Clones are cheap to create, but bonds are not, so even a whisper of a duplicate identity must post its own stake. When clones are detected, slashing seizes the bond, turning the attacker's capital into the penalty. Like a glacier wearing down a false summit before it reaches its zenith, the system needs no perfect detection, only the credible threat that each clone's deposit is forfeit.
